questions.q: What is the defining difference between clustering and classification?
options: Clustering works only on text data
Clustering finds groups without a target label to learn from
Clustering always produces exactly two groups
Clustering requires a separate test set
questions.explain: Clustering is unsupervised: there is no label column, so the algorithm groups rows by similarity alone.

questions.q: Why do we standardize features before running k-means on the customer data?
options: Spend is in the hundreds and visits are in single digits, so spend would dominate the distance calculation
Standardizing guarantees a higher silhouette score
k-means cannot read unscaled numbers
It removes the need to choose the number of clusters
questions.explain: Clustering judges similarity by distance, so a large-scale feature overwhelms a small-scale one unless both are on comparable scales.

questions.q: Which family labels sparse points as noise (label -1) and does not need a cluster count up front?
options: Centroid-based (k-means)
Hierarchical (agglomerative)
Density-based (DBSCAN)
Naive Bayes
questions.explain: DBSCAN treats dense regions as clusters and marks isolated points as noise, needing eps and min_samples instead of a cluster count.

questions.q: The lesson's k-means run scored a silhouette of about 0.77. How should you read that?
options: Points are, on average, much closer to their own cluster than to the next nearest one, so the groups are well separated
The model is 77 percent accurate
77 percent of customers were assigned to the wrong cluster
The number of clusters should be 77
questions.explain: The silhouette score ranges from -1 to 1. Values near 0.7 or higher suggest well-separated clusters. It is not an accuracy.

questions.q: Why should you name clusters by their profile (for example, 'frequent mid-spenders') rather than by their label number?
options: Numbers above 2 are not allowed
Cluster numbers are arbitrary and can change between runs or library versions
Profiles are required by scikit-learn
Label numbers are always sorted by cluster size
questions.explain: The integer labels have no inherent meaning or order, so business names should come from what the group's averages actually show.
